findings.title: A small group of test cells (2 genuinely red) landed in one commit before the implementation commit
findings.evidence: Commit 0e48dacf6 ('test(db): #968 add the batch-cancellation re-issue cells, red against the unconditional refusal') adds four cells to intake-batch.test.mjs in one commit; commit 720d8a55c (the migration) follows 20 seconds later. Per ticket #968's own report, two of the four (`p968.reissue.blocked_canceller_may_be_replaced`, `p968.reissue.excludes_already_committed_child`) were confirmed RED first; the other two (`active_canceller_still_refuses`, `terminal_batch_never_reissued`) were already green pre-migration (guard-rail/regression cells). Read literally, /tdd's rule flags 'a commit that adds a whole battery of red cells before any implementation' as the anti-pattern; here 2 red cells (not 1) land in a single commit ahead of the green commit.
findings.required_fix: No fix required. WORK-ORDER rule 4 explicitly permits 'Commit per green slice or per small group of slices,' and all four cells exercise ONE seam (`clara.cancel_intake_batch`'s one refusal branch) rather than an unrelated battery across many behaviours -- the documented repo standard overrides the stricter one-test-at-a-time reading here. Noted for calibration only.

findings.title: The whole new migration and its whole new 5-cell test battery landed in a single commit
findings.evidence: Commit f049a0d7d ('feat(db): #964 move the document-ingest reservation window to Asia/Kuala_Lumpur') adds migration 0252 (424 lines) AND the new document-ingest-window-myt.test.mjs (221 lines, 5 cells) together. The report asserts red was confirmed manually before the commit ('the file's own before hook threw loudly'), but the git history itself shows no separate red commit.
findings.required_fix: No fix required. The migration is an atomic anchored-splice DDL unit that cannot usefully be committed half-applied, and the report's own prose documents the red-then-green sequence that was actually followed. Consistent with the 'small group of slices' allowance in WORK-ORDER rule 4.

findings.title: 0253_batch_cancel_reissue.sql ships with no dedicated --import preintegration-gate module
findings.evidence: packages/db/package.json's gate chain gains entries only for 0252 (document-ingest-window-myt-preintegration-gate.mjs) and 0254 (intake-refusal-record-preintegration-gate.mjs); 0253 has none. Ticket #968's own new cells instead use an in-file schema_migrations stem probe (`REISSUE_STEM = "batch_cancel_reissue$"`, `reissueReady()`/`gateReissue()` added directly to the already-participating intake-batch.test.mjs).
findings.required_fix: No fix required. This mirrors the EXACT pattern #964 itself uses in the very same file for its own p964.window.capacity_descriptor_myt cell (MYT_WINDOW_STEM/gateMytWindow) -- a new cell added to a file that already participates in the node --test glob and is already gated at the file level (intake-batches-preintegration-gate.mjs) needs only a per-cell frontier check, not a second --import module. Flagged only so a future reviewer does not mistake the omission for a gap without checking this precedent inside the same diff.

findings.title: Two new cells verify a door's contract by reading clara.audit_log directly rather than through a dedicated read door
findings.evidence: p965.refusal.record_names_the_docs_ceiling_firm_file_and_moment (packages/db/tests/intake-refusal-record.test.mjs) and p968.reissue.blocked_canceller_may_be_replaced (packages/db/tests/intake-batch.test.mjs) each run `select ... from clara.audit_log where ...` via rootQuery to assert the door wrote the expected audit rows. Read against /tdd's anti-pattern list alone ('verifying through external means instead of the interface'), this looks like a side-channel check of an internal collaborator.
findings.required_fix: No fix required. `clara.audit_log` is append-only and reading it directly to verify a door's own audit-writing contract is an extremely well-established, repo-wide convention (confirmed via grep across a21-adversarial.test.mjs, binding-proposal-pr-1.test.mjs, f-a2-excision.test.mjs, counterparty-alias-kind.test.mjs and others) for a first-class behaviour of an accounting system (auditability). Per the code-review skill's own rule that a documented repo standard overrides the smell/anti-pattern baseline, this is not flagged as a violation.
